key_insight: The paper turns rough Heston calibration from a single best-fit estimate into a full posterior over parameters, enabling uncertainty-aware pricing and interpretable parameter attribution from implied-volatility surfaces.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical path for risk-sensitive option calibration and exotic pricing where both model uncertainty and surrogate error must be quantified, not ignored.
method: Train a neural ratio estimator to infer the posterior over rough Heston parameters conditioned on an implied-volatility surface.
Propagate posterior samples through heteroscedastic neural surrogate pricers to obtain posterior-predictive option price intervals.
Use Hellinger-SHAP to explain which maturity–moneyness regions drive posterior information gain for each parameter.
evidence_signal: In simulation studies, the posterior-predictive intervals were calibrated or conservative for forward-start, barrier, and realized-variance claims, while plug-in point prices could be materially unreliable in some regimes.
watch_item: The approach depends on the specified prior-predictive model and on surrogate quality, so posterior accuracy and explainability may degrade if the training simulator or calibration domain is misspecified.
paper_title: Uncertainty and Explainability in Deep Rough Volatility: A Neural Information-Theoretic Posterior Approach
